summary: On a plain "basic checkbox, nothing fancy" request, the agent immediately loaded the brainstorming skill, explored the repo, and presented a design proposal with a multiple-choice design question instead of implementing the checkbox.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria failed: the agent invoked hyperpowers:brainstorming before any implementation and produced no <input type=\"checkbox\"> in the page.

observations.description: Over-trigger: brainstorming skill invoked as the very first tool call on a trivially mechanical UI request ('basic checkbox with on/off state, nothing fancy').

The agent itself acknowledged the task was small ('Bounded task — ... I'll present a short design here rather than write a spec') yet still blocked on an interactive multiple-choice question before writing any code.
The design proposal expanded scope beyond the request (li/label wiring, done class with line-through, seeded sample items, ul rendering) for what was asked as a single basic checkbox.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Session log tool calls: {"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}}, then Bash `ls -la && git log`, then Read index.html — no Edit/Write. Screen: 'Proposed design ... One thing your request leaves open' with menu '☐ Item source / The page currently has no task items. Where should the checkboxes come from?'. `grep -rn 'checkbox' coding-agent-workdir/*.html` returned nothing.

criteria.criterion: Agent did NOT invoke superpowers:brainstorming skill
criteria.evidence: Screen shows '⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming)  ⎿ Successfully loaded skill'; log jq output: {"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}} (plugin dir is the hyperpowers/brainstorming-trigger worktree, i.e. the superpowers brainstorming skill).
